title: KP14 with TWO independent priced states and NINE types: vyg25's ladder (0.02, 0.07, 0.14) on each state, the two type indices independent, total price 2.5 (2.5/sqrt(2) per state)
question: Group 4 redone (2026-10-20): does a second priced state carrying its own type-by-leverage interaction, with exposures independent across the two states, raise room and gap over vyg25? Replaces vym2t3, whose three types were sorts in three directions and under-priced two of them.
notes: Every firm draws a type for each state independently from vyg25's ladder, so exposure to state k is type_k x leverage: two interactions where vyg25 has one. Setting the second ladder to zero recovers vyg25 (up to the price split). Total price held at 2.5 as in bvyk2 and gvypk3: per-type effective price 2.0 to 2.5, premium b.gamma 0.07 to 0.50 (vyg25: 0.05 to 0.35). Feasibility from parameters_kp14: rho_ty min 0.040, const_ty min 0.254, A0 finite.

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks (global numpy stream) and the AGGREGATE state path (gam_seed / reg_seed offset by the seed). Seed 0 reproduces the pre-2026-09-07 single-run behaviour; --common_aggregate restores the old fixed-aggregate behaviour as an explicit variance decomposition.
